Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2023. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Liam Chen, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering robust revenue growth across our diversified segments in heavy machinery, precision components, and aftermarket services, while advancing our transformation initiatives, optimizing inventory, expanding regionally, and investing strategically in capacity and innovation. Our book-to-bill remains strong, market share is expanding, and we're guiding higher for the full year amid resilient demand in key end-markets like semiconductors, EVs, and renewables. These results underscore the strength of our positioning in the industrial equipment sector.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Harlan (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Turning to our financial performance, Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. reported total revenue of $2.82 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2023, representing a robust 14.2% increase year-over-year from $2.47 billion in the prior-year period. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, highlighting the resilience of our portfolio and the initial payoffs from our multi-year transformation efforts. Excluding the 2.1% impact from our recent acquisition of Precision Automation Systems, organic revenue grew 12.1% year-over-year, fueled by 8% higher volumes, 4.5% from pricing discipline, and a modest 0.4% tailwind from foreign exchange.

Diving into our core segments aligned with industrial equipment verticals: Heavy Machinery, which comprises 58% of total revenue at $1.64 billion, achieved 16.8% year-over-year growth. This was driven by robust demand for our next-generation electric excavators and autonomous material handling systems, especially in non-residential construction and warehouse automation. Our book-to-bill ratio in this segment reached 1.28 times, improved from 1.15 times a year ago, with backlog surpassing $4.2 billion—our highest level in five years. Shipments of the E-Series electric skid steers, equipped with integrated IoT for fleet telematics, jumped 25% year-over-year, gaining traction as ESG regulations phase out legacy diesel alternatives.

Precision Components, representing 27% of revenue at $761 million, posted 11.3% growth. Aerospace original equipment manufacturer demand was particularly strong, with revenue from turbine blade machining centers rising 19% as Boeing and Airbus increased production on the 737 MAX and A320neo programs. We also benefited from semiconductor fabrication equipment trends, where our high-precision CNC lathes supported U.S. capex spurred by the CHIPS Act. Automotive growth was more muted at 5%, reflecting a slower electric vehicle transition among players like Ford and GM.

Our highest-margin Aftermarket Services segment, at 15% of revenue or $419 million, grew 9.7% year-over-year. This momentum comes from our emphasis on predictive maintenance through the DynamicsAI platform, which uses machine learning on edge-computed sensor data to cut unplanned downtime by as much as 30%. Adoption has accelerated, with 42% of our installed base now connected, up from 28% last year, providing recurring revenue stability.

On a regional basis, performance remained balanced, helping offset some macroeconomic pressures. North America, 52% of revenue at $1.47 billion, expanded 17.5% year-over-year, powered by infrastructure investments under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and onshoring momentum. Data center expansions by hyperscalers such as AWS and Google have lifted demand for our HVAC precision chillers and cleanroom robotics. EMEA, at 24% or $677 million, grew 8.2% despite elevated energy costs tied to the Ukraine situation; our manufacturing footprint in Germany enabled share gains in wind turbine nacelle assembly equipment, countering weaker chemical and pharmaceutical capex. Asia-Pacific contributed 20% or $564 million, up 13.9%, with China rebounding 11% on factory restarts post-COVID—though we're vigilant on property sector risks. India stood out with 28% growth, supported by Production Linked Incentive schemes for electronics manufacturing, where our pick-and-place robots are replacing imports from Fanuc and ABB. Rest of World added 4% with modest 7% growth.

Supporting trends include the Industry 4.0 transition, with McKinsey projecting 15% compound annual growth through 2028 for digital twins and collaborative robots. We've committed $250 million to R&D year-to-date, including Gen-3 welding robots featuring AI vision systems that trimmed cycle times 22% in trials with OEMs like John Deere. Pricing averaged 5.2% across the portfolio, aided by 65% North American content that insulates us from tariffs.

Strategically, we're focusing on high-return levers: boosting aftermarket attach rates to 25% by fiscal year-end 2025 via DynamicsAI subscriptions; accelerating electrification to reach 30% of Heavy Machinery sales as electric by 2026, in line with net-zero goals from Cummins and Caterpillar; and pursuing tuck-in acquisitions in automation software like Precision to build recurring streams.

Gross margins came in at 28.5%, up 120 basis points, driven by these dynamics. Operating expenses were controlled at $650 million, yielding operating income of $225 million. Net income totaled $180 million, or $1.25 per diluted share.

Shifting to inventory levels and our management strategies, which are vital for working capital efficiency and margin protection in this cyclical space. Consolidated inventory ended the quarter at $1.45 billion, up just 3% sequentially from $1.41 billion but down 8% year-over-year from $1.58 billion. This discipline reflects softer end-market demand in areas like non-residential construction and discrete manufacturing. Days inventory outstanding improved to 82 days from 88 days last year and below the 95-day industry average for peers such as Caterpillar and Ingersoll Rand. Annualized inventory turns reached 4.5 times, up from 4.1 times, supporting the margin expansion we saw.

By category, finished goods—mainly high-value skid-steer loaders and precision milling machines—were 42% of total at $610 million, stable sequentially as we cleared excess from the 2022 supply disruptions. Work-in-progress increased 5% to $420 million due to extended lead times on semiconductor inputs for smart factory lines, while raw materials edged up 2% to $420 million from pre-buying steel and aluminum ahead of potential Q4 tariff increases. Year-to-date, we've trimmed inventory 12% from Q1 2023 peaks, surpassing the S&P Industrial Machinery Select Industry Index's 7% average drawdown, freeing $185 million for share repurchases and R&D on electric forging presses.

Regionally, North America is leanest at 75 days outstanding, leveraging reshoring and nearshoring—our Fort Worth site sources 65% of parts within 1,500 miles, dodging Red Sea issues. EMEA inventory is steady at $380 million or 18% of total, with 90 days outstanding, as we manage softer mining capex in South Africa and buffer wind turbine gearbox stock amid EU carbon border adjustments. APAC inventory rose 7% sequentially to $520 million, lifting days to 95; this is intentional given China's 15% drop in concrete batching plant orders, but it hedges Section 301 steel tariff risks that could raise COGS 2-3 points. India and Southeast Asia offset with 20% shipment growth in forklifts and conveyors.

Our approach has advanced with SAP S/4HANA and Blue Yonder AI demand sensing, boosting forecast accuracy 18% to 92% at the SKU level across 15,000 part families, incorporating IoT from 250,000 field assets. Predictive analytics have reduced safety stock and cut obsolescence reserves 25% to $45 million for hydraulic cylinders. Vendor Managed Inventory with Nucor and Timken covers 35% of raw materials on consignment, while blockchain on titanium traceability slashed disputes 40% during steel spikes.

For Q4, we anticipate 80-85 days outstanding, with $50-75 million more reductions via scrap initiatives, setting us up for IIJA-driven road milling demand up 10-15% sequentially. Multi-supplier diversification, digital twins, and optimized distribution keep service levels over 96%.

Expanding on regional revenue dynamics to underscore our diversification: North America at 45% or around $1.27 billion equivalent grew 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, powered by CHIPS and IRA policies. High-precision AxisPro 5-axis mills saw 25% order surges for Intel Ohio and TSMC Arizona, plus $120 million in EV battery lines for Ford and GM equivalents. ASPs held at $2.8 million with Predictive Maintenance AI bundles cutting downtime 30%, backlog up 22% to $2.1 billion, margins +220 bps to 28%.

Europe, 28% or $790 million adjusted, grew 9% amid energy woes and ECB hikes, outperforming IDC's 2-3% regional forecast. EcoWeld robots for VW Salzgitter and Siemens turbines added €80 million, Frankfurt demos converting 40%, though ASPs softened 2% to €1.9 million—countered by Polish assembly ramping Q4. Backlog up 12% to €650 million, Nexus IoT targeting 25% H2 margins via 18% energy savings.

Asia-Pacific, 24% or $677 million, surged 22% on China recovery and India PLI, with $150 million RoboDrill bookings for Samsung Vietnam and Foxconn India. China hit 35% regional share despite controls, ASPs +6% to $1.5 million on edge AI yields. Backlog +35% to $900 million, Singapore hub adapting for seismic needs.

Rest of World, 3% or $85 million, up 5% on Petrobras Brazil rigs and Aramco Saudi upgrades, plus Mexico auto presses at 32% margins.

This balance—now 45/28/24/3 versus 50/25/20/5 two years ago—de-risks volatility, growing faster than Rockwell or ABB via modular software premiums. FY24 capex at $150 million expands regional fabs, Nexus AI/ML accelerates ROI 25%, Reliance MoU eyes hydrogen.

On capital expenditure plans and priorities for FY24 into FY25, we're guiding $450 million total, up 12% from $402 million last year, or 4.2% of revenue run-rate, aligned with Haas and DMG Mori. $320 million deployed through Q3, $130 million back-half heavy.

Capacity expansion takes 45% or $202 million: Spartanburg CNC hub gets $85 million for 25% more machining on EV stators and EUV tools, adding Okuma mills and Fanuc tenders for 30% throughput gains. Dortmund hydraulic presses allocate $45 million for REPowerEU wind nacelles from Vestas/Siemens, dodging 25-35% tariffs.

Automation/digital: 30% or $135 million, with $60 million FactoryTalk-ApexEdge AI predicting failures 92% accurately, cutting downtime 18%; $40 million UR10e cobots for Amazon-like fulfillment; $35 million Siemens NX digital twins optimizing Kalamazoo welds 15%, saving 200 tons steel.

Sustainability: 15% or $68 million, $30 million BYD forklifts slashing diesel 40%, $25 million servo presses for 50% efficiency, ENERGY STAR compliant.

Maintenance/supply chain: 10% or $45 million, qualifying U.S. linear guides to cut Asia BOM from 40% to 25%, lead times 26 to 8 weeks. North America 55% ($248M), EMEA 30% ($135M), APAC 15% ($67M).

FY25 signals $500-550 million, shifting to digital twins 40% and $100 million+ additive hybrids with GE-like partners. Targeting 18-22% IRR.

Regarding macroeconomic impacts on end-market demand, ISM PMI at 48.5 pressured orders down 12% to $1.2 billion, but book-to-bill rose to 1.05x, backlog $2.8 billion. Fed rates at 5.25-5.50% deferred capex, U.S. industrial spending +1.8%, hitting material handling 18%. Capex Optimization Suites captured 15% orders with 18-month paybacks.

Inflation at 3.2% supported 6.5% pricing, margins 42.5%; Red Sea added 4-6 weeks, mitigated by Monterrey nearshore cutting China to 12%. North America semis +28% on CHIPS, autos -10%; Europe wind -22% offset by hydrogen; APAC high-tech +35% despite property; emerging +14%.

Electrification +19%, aerospace +25%, automation +8% on labor gaps. Mix now 35% semis (up), 25% auto (down), 12% renewables. Dynashield subscriptions target $100 million ARR by 2026.

On market share, we gained 150 basis points globally to 13.8% in $285 billion market per Gardner, outpacing AMT's 2.1%. Metalworking/CNC +220 bps to 16.2% on ApexFlex AI mills, $150 million EV contract displacing rivals. Automation +180 bps to 14.5% on RoboForge uptime vs. Fanuc/ABB. Material handling -50 bps to 11.2% on Chinese pricing, but telehandlers flat 19%.

North America +250 bps to 18.4% on reshoring, $220 million semi/cleanroom. EMEA -80 bps to 12.1%, offset Nordics wind. APAC +100 bps to 9.7%, India/SE Asia +300 bps. LatAm +400 bps to 4.5% on Brazil mining.

Tech-first R&D 12%, ApexCloud IoT, dual rare earths stabilize 14-week leads. Target 200 bps FY24 gain.

For guidance, Q4 revenue 11-13% year-over-year growth, full-year raised to $11.0-11.3 billion, 13%+. Q3 equivalent framing: $680-710 million adjusted, 8-13% sequential, 12% YoY midpoint, book-to-bill 1.15x, backlog $2.8 billion.

Machinery $375-390 million +15% volumes; automation $205-215 million EV pull; services $100-105 million IoT. North America 18% YoY, EMEA mid-single, APAC offset China. MaaS pilot $15 million.

Full-year $2.65-2.72 billion adjusted context, 6-9% growth, EBITDA 22.5%. Machinery 7-10%, automation 9-12%, services 8%. $180 million CapEx scales 5-axis edge computing.

Finally, on dividend policy: Quarterly $0.65 per share declared, payable December 15 to November 25 record, annualized $2.60 up 4%, yield 2.81% at $92.50 stock vs. sector 2.4%, ahead Caterpillar 1.6%, Deere 1.5%. Payout 40-50% adjusted earnings, TTM 44%, FCF 105% conversion $1.25 billion.

10-year CAGR 8.2%, backed by IIJA North America dozers, EMEA cranes, APAC semis. Balance sheet net debt/EBITDA 1.8x, $1.1 billion liquidity. Sustain 5-7% growth, Smart Factory 250 bps margins. $2 billion buyback, $450 million YTD, M&A electrification.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value.

Now, I will hand over to Maria Gonzalez, COO, for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez (COO):
Thank you, John. Operationally, we've prioritized manufacturing process optimization, supply chain efficiency, and customer service enhancements. Building on our inventory discipline, we've leveraged digital technologies like SAP-integrated AI forecasting and IoT analytics to achieve 96% service levels, while VMI and blockchain ensure resilience against disruptions. Employee health and safety metrics are best-in-class, with zero lost-time incidents across our global plants. We're also advancing nearshoring, with Mexico facilities reducing lead times 30%, and sustainability efforts like electrified fleets cutting emissions 40%.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Liam Chen, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Liam Chen (CTO):
Thank you, Maria. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing heavily in research and development in artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, and the Internet of Things. Our DynamicsAI platform and E-Series electric skid steers with IoT telematics are revolutionizing predictive maintenance and fleet management, reducing downtime 30% and capturing share in ESG-driven markets. New Gen-3 welding robots with AI vision have cut cycle times 22%, and ApexFlex 5-axis mills with toolpath optimization boost throughput 25%. Our new DynamicsAI predictive maintenance suite is significantly impacting the market, with 42% installed base adoption driving recurring revenues and 20% higher customer retention.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new DynamicsAI platform on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thanks, Ben. DynamicsAI is a game-changer for our aftermarket and services recurring streams. With machine learning on edge sensors reducing downtime up to 30%, we've hit 42% adoption on our installed base, up sharply, and target 25% attach rates by FY25 end. This high-margin software layer—92% predictive accuracy in pilots—boosts overall profitability by 200-300 basis points through subscriptions, while enhancing OEM pull-through in heavy machinery and precision components. Long-term, it supports 15% CAGR in services amid Industry 4.0, with early $100 million ARR trajectory, directly lifting EPS mid-teens into 2025 as EV and semi ramps accelerate.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

John Harlan:
Good question, Lisa. For full-year 2024, we're guiding $11.0-11.3 billion, implying 13%+ growth, with Q4 at 11-13% year-over-year. This reflects backlog conversion from $4.2 billion+, 1.25x book-to-bill, and tailwinds in semis, EVs, and renewables offsetting China caution. Segment-wise, heavy machinery mid-teens on electrification, precision components double-digits on aero/semi, aftermarket 10%+ on DynamicsAI. Regional drivers: North America 17%+, APAC 14%, EMEA 8%. Upside from IIJA, CHIPS; disciplined pricing 4-5%, CapEx $450 million scaling capacity. Risks like input inflation hedged by inventory at 80-85 DIO.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel (Morgan Stanley):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Alex Rivera:
Absolutely, Mike. Our geographic diversification to 45/28/24/3 mix de-risks us while capturing growth. North America leads with Spartanburg and Fort Worth expansions under CHIPS/IIJA, targeting 18%+ revenue share gains. EMEA leverages Dortmund/Frankfurt/Poland for EU Green Deal, wind, and aero. APAC doubles down on Singapore/Suzhou/India JVs for PLI semis/EVs, gaining 300 bps in India/SE Asia. LatAm/Mexico nearshoring adds Monterrey for USMCA auto/mining. $450 million CapEx prioritizes localization, reducing Asia BOM 15 points, with $150 million regional fabs. Backlog visibility supports 13%+ FY24 growth, eyeing $500 million+ FY25 CapEx for additive and digital twins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Maria Gonzalez:
Thanks, Rachel. Energy pressures from Ukraine and inflation are real, but our strategies mitigate effectively. Digital twins and Nexus IoT optimize usage 18% real-time across plants; electrified fleets like BYD forklifts cut diesel 40%, with $68 million CapEx targeting 50% efficiency in servo presses. Localized manufacturing in Germany/Poland/Mexico shrinks transit emissions/fuel, while AI predictive maintenance trims idle times 18%. EMEA margins held via hedging; overall, sustainability CapEx yields 20%+ IRR, aligning with ESG mandates and insulating 200 bps potential CBAM hits. Service levels stay 96%+.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
